types.name: WaxWindowOptions
types.title: WaxWindowOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Window takes.

props.name: title
props.text: "Window" when omitted.

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name shown before the title. The menu's Icons page lists the names.

props.name: width
props.text: Default 340, or 520 with side navigation.

props.name: height
props.text: Default 420, or 380 with pages.

props.name: closable
props.text: False leaves out the close button.

props.name: visible
props.text: False creates the window hidden.

props.name: nav
props.text: Gives the window pages, listed down the side or along the top.

props.name: nav_width
props.text: Width of the side navigation column.

props.name: remember
props.text: False stops Wax remembering the window's position and size between sessions.

types.name: WaxPageOptions
types.title: WaxPageOptions
types.text: The options that window:Page takes.

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name shown before the page's name. The menu's Icons page lists the names.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, { icon = "text" })

props.name: bottom
props.text: Lists the page at the bottom of a side navigation column.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, { bottom = true })

props.name: scroll
props.text: False makes a page that does not scroll. Its controls stack from the top, and a Grid or Console with no height takes the space left.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, { scroll = true })

types.name: WaxPage
types.title: WaxPage
types.text: A page of a window that has navigation. It is a container for controls.
types.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)

signals.name: NearEnd
signals.text: Fires while the end of the page is in view: when the user scrolls close to the bottom, and a few times a second while the page is not full. Add more content in the handler, or do nothing when there is no more.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)
page.NearEnd:Connect(function()
    print("NearEnd")
end)

types.name: WaxWindow
types.title: WaxWindow
types.text: A window in the menu. Controls added to it go into its body, or into a first page called "Main" when it has pages.
types.use: local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })

signals.name: Opened
signals.text: Fires when the window is shown.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.Opened:Connect(function()
    print("Opened")
end)

signals.name: Closed
signals.text: Fires when the window is hidden.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.Closed:Connect(function()
    print("Closed")
end)

signals.name: PageChanged
signals.text: Fires with the name of the page that was selected.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.PageChanged:Connect(function(name)
    print(name)
end)

funcs.name: SetTitle
funcs.text: Changes the text in the title bar.

funcs.name: SetPosition
funcs.text: Moves the window, keeping it on the screen.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetPosition(x, y)

funcs.name: SetSize
funcs.text: Resizes the window, no smaller than its minimum size.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetSize(width, height)

funcs.name: SetNavWidth
funcs.text: Sets the width of the navigation column of a window made with nav = "side".

funcs.name: Show
funcs.text: Shows the window, in front of the others.

funcs.name: Hide
funcs.text: Hides the window. Hiding the last one closes the menu.

funcs.name: SetVisible
funcs.text: Shows or hides the window.

funcs.name: IsVisible
funcs.text: True while the window is shown.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local result = window:IsVisible()

funcs.name: SetMinimized
funcs.text: Minimises the window to its title bar, or restores it.

funcs.name: IsMinimized
funcs.text: True while the window is minimised.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local result = window:IsMinimized()

funcs.name: StatusBar
funcs.text: Adds a status line along the bottom of the window, or returns the one the window already has. `text` sets its message.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)

funcs.name: Destroy
funcs.text: Removes the window and everything on it.

funcs.name: Page
funcs.text: Adds a page to a window made with nav = "side" or "top". The first page added is selected.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)

funcs.name: RemovePage
funcs.text: Removes a page made with Page, with everything on it.

funcs.name: SelectPage
funcs.text: Switches to the page with this name.

types.name: WaxStatusOptions
types.title: WaxStatusOptions
types.text: The options that statusBar:Set takes.

props.name: kind
props.text: Sets the colour of the text and the icon. "info" when omitted.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Set(message, { kind = "info" })

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name shown before the text. The menu's Icons page lists the names.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Set(message, { icon = "text" })

types.name: WaxStatusBar
types.title: WaxStatusBar
types.text: The line along the bottom of a window that Window:StatusBar returns.
types.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)

funcs.name: Set
funcs.text: Shows a message and removes the busy indicator.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Set(message, options)

funcs.name: Busy
funcs.text: Shows a message with a turning indicator beside it, until the next Set.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Busy(message)

funcs.name: Progress
funcs.text: Shows a thin progress line across the top of the bar. `amount` is 0..1, and nil hides the line.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Progress(amount)

funcs.name: Right
funcs.text: Shows text at the right-hand end of the bar.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Right(message)

funcs.name: Clear
funcs.text: Empties the message and hides the progress line.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)
statusBar:Clear()

types.name: WaxOverlayOptions
types.title: WaxOverlayOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Overlay takes.

props.name: anchor
props.text: Where on the screen the panel is pinned. "top-right" when omitted.

props.name: x
props.text: Distance in from the anchor's edge. Default 16.

props.name: y
props.text: Distance in from the anchor's edge. Default 16.

props.name: width
props.text: Default 240.

props.name: title
props.text: Adds a heading.

props.name: background
props.text: False leaves out the panel behind the controls.

props.name: movable
props.text: False stops the player dragging it while the menu is open. Where it was dragged to is remembered.

types.name: WaxOverlay
types.title: WaxOverlay
types.text: A panel pinned to the screen that stays up during play and never takes the mouse.
types.use: local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)

signals.name: Scrolled
signals.text: On a panel made with ui.Panel: the wheel was turned over it, 1 for down and -1 for up. The game does not see the wheel while the mouse is over a panel.
signals.use:
local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)
overlay.Scrolled:Connect(function(steps)
    print(steps)
end)

funcs.name: SetVisible
funcs.text: Shows or hides the overlay.

funcs.name: IsVisible
funcs.text: True while the overlay is shown.
funcs.use:
local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)
local result = overlay:IsVisible()

funcs.name: SetAnchor
funcs.text: Pins the overlay somewhere else. x and y keep their values when omitted.
funcs.use:
local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)
overlay:SetAnchor(anchor, x, y)

funcs.name: Destroy
funcs.text: Removes the overlay and everything on it.

funcs.name: SetOffset
funcs.text: Moves it without changing its anchor. x and y keep their values when omitted.

funcs.name: IsShowing
funcs.text: True while it is really on screen: switched on, and what it waits for (the menu, the mouse) is there.
funcs.use:
local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)
local result = overlay:IsShowing()

types.name: WaxPanelOptions
types.title: WaxPanelOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Panel takes.

props.name: when
props.text: When it shows: "cursor" (the default) while the Wax menu is open or one of the game's own screens has the mouse, "menu" only with the Wax menu, "always" whenever it is switched on.

props.name: padding
props.text: Space between its edge and its controls.

props.name: height
props.text: A fixed height. As tall as its controls when omitted.

props.name: zoom
props.text: Draws everything in it this much larger (1.25 is a quarter larger). Text stays sharp.

props.name: opacity
props.text: How solid its background is, 0 to 1. 0.96 when omitted.

props.name: visible
props.text: False makes it hidden until SetVisible(true).

props.name: on_press
props.text: Runs when the panel is pressed where it has no control.
props.use: local overlay = ui.Panel({ on_press = function() end })

types.name: WaxFitOptions
types.title: WaxFitOptions
types.text: The options that ui.FitGame takes.

props.name: scale
props.text: How large the game's menus are drawn, 0.5 to 1. 0.85 when omitted.

props.name: corner
props.text: The corner they shrink towards. "bottom-left" when omitted, which frees the right and the top.

props.name: x
props.text: Moves them sideways after they are made smaller, as a share of the screen. Right is positive.

props.name: y
props.text: Moves them up or down after they are made smaller, as a share of the screen. Down is positive.

props.name: enabled
props.text: False makes the request wait for SetEnabled(true).

types.name: WaxFit
types.title: WaxFit
types.text: A request to draw the game's own menus smaller.
types.use: local fit = ui.FitGame(options)

funcs.name: Set

params.name: x
params.text: Keeps its value when omitted.

params.name: y
params.text: Keeps its value when omitted.

funcs.use:
local fit = ui.FitGame(options)
fit:Set(scale, x, y)

funcs.name: Remove
funcs.text: Gives the game's menus their own size back.

funcs.name: Check
funcs.text: The game path of a picture as it can be shown ("/Game/.../ITEM_Wood.ITEM_Wood"), or nil when the text is not one.

funcs.name: Stats

returns.type: { loaded: integer, failed: integer, waiting: integer, pinned: integer, worst_ms: number }

funcs.text: How many game pictures were loaded, failed, are waiting and are kept in memory.

types.name: WaxNotifyOptions
types.title: WaxNotifyOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Notify takes.

props.name: title
props.text: A bold line above the text.

props.name: kind
props.text: Sets the colour and the icon. "info" when omitted.

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name used in place of the kind's own. The menu's Icons page lists the names.

props.name: seconds
props.text: Time on screen. Default 4, and 0 keeps it until closed.

props.name: progress
props.text: 0..1. Shows progress in place of the countdown and keeps the notification until closed.

types.name: WaxNotification
types.title: WaxNotification
types.text: What ui.Notify gives back.
types.use: local notification = ui.Notify(text, options)

funcs.name: SetText
funcs.text: Replaces the text.

funcs.name: SetTitle
funcs.text: Replaces the title. Does nothing on a notification made without one.

funcs.name: SetProgress
funcs.text: Shows how far a task is, 0..1, in place of the countdown. The notification then stays until closed.

funcs.name: Close
funcs.text: Closes the notification.

funcs.name: SetCorner
funcs.text: Moves notifications to another corner of the screen, closing the ones showing.

funcs.name: SetLimit
funcs.text: Sets how many notifications show at once (at least 1).

funcs.name: Clear
funcs.text: Closes every notification.

funcs.name: Count
funcs.text: How many notifications are showing.

types.name: WaxIcons
types.title: ui.Icons
types.text: Icon names: the bundled Lucide set ("shield", "wrench", "map-pin" ...) plus images that mods register.

funcs.name: Names
funcs.text: Every icon name, sorted. The menu's Icons page shows them.

funcs.name: Has
funcs.text: True when there is an icon with this name.

funcs.name: Find
funcs.text: Names containing the text, at most `limit` of them (every name when the text is empty).

funcs.name: Register
funcs.text: Adds an icon from a PNG file. White on transparent works best, because the icon is tinted when drawn.

types.name: WaxDebugPanel
types.title: ui.Debug
types.text: The in-game debug panel.

funcs.name: Page
funcs.text: Adds a page to the debug panel for the calling mod. The page is removed when the mod reloads.

funcs.name: Window
funcs.text: The debug panel's window, or nil while the panel is not running.

funcs.name: Show
funcs.text: Shows the debug panel and opens the menu.

types.name: WaxUI
types.title: ui
types.text: The GUI library: the menu (windows you click), overlays (panels you only read) and notifications.

props.name: Icons
props.text: Icon names: the bundled Lucide set ("shield", "wrench", "map-pin" ...) plus images that mods register.

props.name: Debug
props.text: The in-game debug panel.

signals.name: Opened
signals.text: Fires when the menu opens.

signals.name: Closed
signals.text: Fires when the menu closes.

signals.name: KeyChanged
signals.text: Fires with the new menu key.

signals.name: ThemeChanged
signals.text: Fires with the theme's name after SetTheme or ResetTheme.

signals.name: ScreenChanged
signals.text: Fires when ScreenSize gives another answer: a new resolution or interface scale.

funcs.name: Open

params.name: options
params.text: `windows = false` frees the mouse for panels only and leaves the windows hidden.

funcs.text: Opens the menu: windows appear and the mouse is freed to use them.

funcs.name: Close
funcs.text: Closes the menu and gives the mouse back to the game.

funcs.name: Toggle
funcs.text: Opens the menu when it is closed, and closes it when it is open.

funcs.name: Copy
funcs.text: Puts text on the clipboard, for pasting anywhere.

funcs.name: IsOpen
funcs.text: True while the menu is open.

funcs.name: SetPreview
funcs.text: Shows the windows without taking the mouse (for screenshots and for looking while you play).

funcs.name: IsPreview
funcs.text: True while the windows are shown in preview.

funcs.name: SetToggleKey
funcs.text: Sets the key that opens and closes the menu, by the engine's key name ("F8"). nil leaves the menu without a key.

funcs.name: GetToggleKey
funcs.text: The key that opens and closes the menu.

funcs.name: Window
funcs.text: Creates a window in the menu. It is removed again when the mod reloads.

funcs.name: Overlay
funcs.text: Creates a panel pinned to the screen that stays up during play and lets clicks through.

funcs.name: Panel
funcs.text: Creates a panel whose controls take the mouse. It has no title bar and shows beside the game's own screens.

funcs.name: Hovered
funcs.text: The value of the slot under the mouse, then its look and its Slots control. Nothing when no slot is under it.

funcs.name: IsTyping
funcs.text: True while a text box of Wax has the keyboard.

funcs.name: ScreenSize
funcs.text: The size of the screen in the units windows and panels are laid out in. While the game is starting and has no screen yet, the answer is 1920 by 1080; ScreenChanged fires if the real one turns out different.

funcs.name: FitGame
funcs.text: Draws the game's own menus (inventory, crafting, benches) smaller, which leaves room beside them for panels. They keep working as before. The request ends when the mod reloads.

funcs.name: GameScreen
funcs.text: The game's own menu screen that is showing now: "UMG_MainMenu", "UMG_EscapeMenu", or a bench or container such as "UMG_Processor_C". For the main menu the second value is its tab: 0 inventory, 1 crafting, 2 tech tree, 3 talents, 4 map. Nothing when none shows.

funcs.name: Tag

params.name: target
params.type: WaxInstance|{ X: number, Y: number, Z: number }

funcs.text: Puts a line of text over an actor, over one part of an actor, or on a spot in the world. It follows what it is on, shows through walls, and tags that would cover each other pile up. The tag goes away by itself when the actor does.

funcs.name: Notify
funcs.text: Shows a short message in a corner of the screen. Sending the same message again restarts the one already showing.

funcs.name: Windows
funcs.text: A list of every window.

funcs.name: Hotkey

params.name: key
params.text: An engine key name such as "F6", "K" or "MiddleMouseButton" (a Keybind control gives you these). It can be held with Ctrl, Shift or Alt: "Ctrl+Three", "Ctrl+Shift+K".

funcs.text: Runs `callback` when the key is pressed during play. The hotkey is removed when the mod reloads.
funcs.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, options)

funcs.name: MinScale
funcs.text: The smallest scale that still draws text at a readable size on this screen.

funcs.name: SetScale
funcs.text: Sets the interface size, where 1 is normal. The size is kept between ui.MinScale() and 2, and the size applied is returned.

funcs.name: GetScale
funcs.text: The interface size in use.

funcs.name: SetTheme
funcs.text: Switches to a named theme, or changes single settings from a table. Everything on screen takes the new colours in place, so no window is rebuilt and no mod is reloaded. Sizes and shapes apply to what is built afterwards.

funcs.name: ResetTheme
funcs.text: Puts every theme setting back to the "Midnight" defaults.

funcs.name: Themes
funcs.text: The names of the built-in themes, then of the ones added with AddTheme.

funcs.name: AddTheme
funcs.text: Adds a theme: a table with any of the colour settings (window, panel, raised, text, accent ...) as "#RRGGBB".

funcs.name: ThemeName
funcs.text: The name of the theme in use.

funcs.name: Color
funcs.text: Makes a colour from "#RRGGBB" or 0xRRGGBB, with an optional alpha of 0..1.

funcs.name: Theme
funcs.text: The table of the theme in use. Its colours follow the theme, so pass them as they are (color = ui.Theme().accent).

funcs.name: AddSettings
funcs.text: Adds the menu's own settings (key, theme, accent, animation, size) to a container, such as a "Settings" page.

types.name: WaxTagOptions
types.title: WaxTagOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Tag takes.

props.name: within
props.text: Metres. Farther away than this the tag is not shown. Default 100.

props.name: lift
props.text: How far above the thing's middle the tag sits, in centimetres. Worked out from the thing when omitted.

types.name: WaxTag
types.title: WaxTag
types.text: A line of text that stays over something in the world.
types.use: local tag = ui.Tag(target, options)

props.name: Instance
props.text: What the tag is on. nil for a tag on a spot.

funcs.name: Remove
funcs.text: Takes the tag off. Safe to call twice, and after the thing it was on is gone.

types.name: WaxHotkeyOptions
types.title: WaxHotkeyOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Hotkey takes.

props.name: in_menu
props.text: Also reacts while the menu is open (off by default, so that typing in a box does not trigger it).
props.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, { in_menu = true })

props.name: typing
props.text: Also reacts while a text box has the keyboard (for a key meant for the box, such as Tab).
props.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, { typing = true })

props.name: hover
props.text: Makes it a key for the slot under the mouse: it only reacts while a slot is under it.
props.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, { hover = true })

types.name: WaxHotkey
types.title: WaxHotkey
types.text: What ui.Hotkey gives back.
types.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, options)

funcs.name: Disconnect
funcs.text: Stops the hotkey.
funcs.use:
local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, options)
hotkey.Disconnect()

funcs.name: SetKey
funcs.text: Changes the key it reacts to.
funcs.use:
local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, options)
hotkey:SetKey(key)

types.name: WaxControl
types.title: WaxControl
types.text: What every control has.
types.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local control = window:Toggle("Example")

signals.name: Changed
signals.text: Fires when the user changes the control's value.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local control = window:Toggle("Example")
control.Changed:Connect(function(...)
    print(...)
end)

funcs.name: Destroy
funcs.text: Removes the control.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local control = window:Toggle("Example")
control:Destroy()

funcs.name: SetVisible
funcs.text: Shows or hides the control. A hidden control takes no room.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local control = window:Toggle("Example")
control:SetVisible(shown)

funcs.name: SetEnabled
funcs.text: Greys the control out and stops it reacting, or makes it usable again.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local control = window:Toggle("Example")
control:SetEnabled(enabled)

types.name: WaxLabelOptions
types.title: WaxLabelOptions
types.text: The options that container:Label takes.

props.name: dim
props.text: Uses the theme's secondary text colour.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local label = window:Label(content, { dim = true })

props.name: color
props.text: A colour in the linear form the engine uses. Make one with ui.Color.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local label = window:Label(content, { color = value })

props.name: size
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })

A field path is a field's name, with a dot for each step into a struct or an array: "RequiredMillijoules", "Requirement.RowName", "Inputs.Element.RowName". Naming a struct or an array of structs asks for everything inside it. A wrong path raises an error that suggests the right one. Rows are read once and kept. Enum fields are read only when their own path is named, and they read as numbers. Maps, sets, delegates, doubles and references to live objects are never read. funcs.name: Fields
funcs.text: The fields of a row as the game declares them. With `path`, the fields of the struct at that field path.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
local dataFields = dataTable:Fields(path)

funcs.name: Meta
funcs.text: The table's meta table, or nil when it has none. Its rows have the same names and say which expansion a row belongs to (RequiredFeatureLevel) and whether the game has retired it (bIsDeprecated).
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
local result = dataTable:Meta()

funcs.name: Stamp
funcs.text: The table's row count and address as text, such as "2215:0x1F3A2B40". It is checked against the game each time. Keep it beside anything you worked out from the table: a different stamp means the table is not the one you read.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
local result = dataTable:Stamp()

types.name: WaxData
types.title: game.Data
types.text: The game's data tables as plain Lua values: recipes, items, creatures, talents and the rest. Nothing is read until you ask, and what was read is kept, so asking twice costs nothing. Text is kept in the language the game was showing when it was read. After the player changes the language it shows in the new one only after Flush, or when the game starts again.

signals.name: Changed
signals.text: Fires when the game has made a table again and what was read from it was dropped. `name` is the table's name, or nil when everything was dropped. Flush fires it too, with no name.

funcs.name: Table
funcs.text: A table by name, with or without the "D_" in front. Letter case does not matter. A wrong name raises an error that suggests the right one.

funcs.name: GetTables
funcs.text: The name of every table the game has, sorted.

funcs.name: Has
funcs.text: True when the game has a table of this name.

funcs.name: Resolve

returns.name: table
returns.text: The table the row is in.

funcs.text: The row a row handle points at, and the table it is in. Nil when the handle points at nothing or at a row the game does not have. A handle whose DataTableName was not read as a name raises an error. Read such a row with Table and Row.

funcs.name: Flush
funcs.text: Forgets everything that was read, so the next read asks the game again. Use it after the player changes the game's language. Rows handed out before stay as they are and are no longer filled in. Changed fires at the end of the frame, so every mod that keeps something worked out from rows can work it out again.

types.name: WaxDataRow
types.title: WaxDataRow
types.text: One row of a data table as plain Lua values, shaped like the game's own data files with every default filled in. `Name` is the row's name. A struct is a table and an array is a list. A name, a string and a text are Lua strings. A reference to an asset is its path, or nil when it points at nothing (false inside a list). A row is shared by everyone who reads it, so never change one.

types.name: globals
types.title: Global functions
types.text: Functions and values every mod has. Use them by name, with nothing in front.

props.name: raw
props.text: The real global table: unguarded access to everything UE4SS offers, including what Wax blocks.

funcs.name: print
funcs.text: Logs the values, joined by tabs, at info level on the mod's channel.

funcs.name: persist
funcs.text: Returns the value kept under `key`, storing `default` (or a new table) on first use. The value survives reloads of the mod.

funcs.name: require
funcs.text: Loads a file of this mod and returns what it returned. `require(mod.Utils)` and `require("Utils")` are the same file, as are `require(mod.extras.Utils)` and `require("extras.Utils")`. A folder with an init.lua is loaded by the folder's name. `require("@Id")` gives another mod's exports.

types.name: blocked
types.title: Blocked functions
types.text: These UE4SS functions raise an error when a mod calls them. The reason is given for each one.

funcs.name: LoopAsync
funcs.text: Blocked in Wax mods: it runs Lua on another thread, which corrupts the game's Lua state. Use task.spawn or task.delay.
